name: mongolid-documenter
description: Write and update the Mongolid library behavior documentation in docs/docs (Docusaurus). Use when asked to document, update, or review docs for Mongolid features, or when source code in src/ changes public behavior.
---

# Mongolid documentation

`docs/docs/` is the official, human-readable description of how the Mongolid library behaves for its users. 
The site is built with Docusaurus (`docs/`) and published by CI. 
Developers review the docs in a pull request before merge. 
Your output is a draft for that review, so be accurate and conservative.

## Source of truth

1. The code in `src/` and the tests in `tests/` define behavior. Read them before writing.
2. Existing docs in `docs/docs/` define style and terminology. Keep both consistent.
3. If code and existing docs disagree, do not silently pick one. Report the conflict in your final summary.
4. Never document behavior you cannot confirm in code or tests. Do not invent options, method names, or defaults.

## Scope

Document **library behavior** only:
- Public API a user calls (models, relations, query builder, cursor, casting, mass assignment, soft delete, events, schema, cache, sequences, and so on).
- Configuration users must set, such as the connection, collection name, and casts.
- Observable behavior, edge cases, and errors users may hit.
- Legacy behavior that is still supported, such as `LegacyRecord` and `HasLegacyAttributesTrait`.

Do not document:
- Internal classes or private methods, unless they are part of the public API.
- Development process, contributing steps, or CI details (those belong in CONTRIBUTING or the README).
- Speculative future features or TODOs.

## Page mapping

Map code to pages. Create a new page only when no existing page fits.

| Page | Code |
|---|---|
| `quick-start.md` | `Connection/`, `Container/`, `Model/AbstractModel.php` |
| `operations.md` | `Query/Builder.php`, `Query/BulkWrite.php`, `DataMapper/` |
| `mass-assignments.md` | `Model/HasAttributesTrait.php` |
| `casting.md` | `Model/Casts/` |
| `converting.md` | `toArray` in `Model/HasAttributesTrait.php` |
| `relationships/embeds.md` | `Model/Relations/EmbedsOne.php`, `EmbedsMany` |
| `relationships/references.md` | `Model/Relations/ReferencesOne.php`, `ReferencesMany` |
| `cursor.md` | `Cursor/` |
| `legacy/*.md` | `LegacyRecord.php`, `HasLegacyAttributesTrait.php`, `HasLegacyRelationsTrait.php` |
| `troubleshooting.md` | Installation and environment issues |

Features with no page yet (soft delete, schema, events, eager loading cache, sequences) need a new page. Use an existing page as a template. The sidebar is autogenerated from the folder structure, so do not edit `sidebars.js` by hand.

## File format

- Start every page with Docusaurus front matter, including `sidebar_position` (use an unused number). Subfolders may use `_category_.json`.
- Use one `# Title` heading per page, then `##` for sections and `###` for subsections.
- Use fenced code blocks with the `php` language tag for code samples.
- Use `:::info` or `:::warning` admonitions sparingly, for important caveats.
- Keep the existing spelling of technical terms: `Model`, `Embeds`, `References`, `Cursor`, `DateTime`, `ObjectId`.

## Writing style

- Write in English, matching the existing docs.
- Use short sentences, direct instructions, and the second person ("you").
- Start each section with what the feature does, then show a minimal example, then describe edge cases.
- Every code example must be valid for the current version of the library. Prefer examples that appear in the tests.
- Do not use filler, marketing language, or unnecessary repetition.

## Verification checklist

Before finishing, confirm each item:
- [ ] Every method, property, option, and default you wrote exists in `src/`.
- [ ] Every code example matches a signature in `src/` or a usage in `tests/`.
- [ ] Links between pages point to existing files.
- [ ] Front matter is present and valid YAML.
- [ ] No internal-only details leaked into the page.
- [ ] Unrelated pages were not modified.

When feasible, validate the docs build:

```bash
cd docs && npm ci && npm run build
```

Do not run the PHP test suite just to validate docs. 
Use it only to confirm a behavior you are unsure about, with the smallest targeted filter, for example `vendor/bin/phpunit --filter <Name>`.

## Output

When you finish, report:
1. Files created or changed, with a one-line reason for each.
2. Behaviors you documented, and the code or test that supports each one.
3. Any conflicts between code and docs, and any gaps you could not confirm.

Do not commit or push unless the user asks. The developer reviews the diff in the pull request.
